## What you can do and ask for

1. **Use the condition report.** The cleaning test is judged against it [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
   - Check what the start-of-tenancy report says about the floor coverings.
   - Renters were meant to complete and sign their part within 5 business days of moving in. Photos are encouraged [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
2. **Gather photos.** The condition report form says photos should be taken at the start and end of the tenancy. They should be dated, labelled with the room or location, and show both close-up detail and the wider view [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). Take dated photos of the carpets now.
3. **Attend the final inspection.** The agent must complete the end-of-tenancy report within 10 days after the agreement ends and give you an opportunity to attend. They must allow for fair wear and tear [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
4. **Ask the agent to point to the basis for the demand.** Ask which clause and which condition-report entry they rely on. A cleaning claim against your bond must be for the reasonable cost of cleaning where the premises weren't left reasonably clean, having regard to their condition at the start [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
5. **If they claim your bond:**
   - They must give you bond claim evidence at least 3 days before claiming the bond for themselves. That evidence must not conflict with a statement in the condition report [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - If you dispute the claim, tell the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority in writing within 14 days after notice that the claim is subject to a Tribunal application [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - A provider's Tribunal application for the bond must also include supporting evidence that doesn't conflict with the condition report [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
6. **Challenge the clause.** You can apply to the Tribunal (VCAT) to have a term declared invalid or varied if it is harsh or unconscionable [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

**Sources used:** the *Residential Tenancies Act 1997* (file "rta-1997-v115-2026-10-13.pdf", dated 13 Oct 2026). Its metadata gives the version as **115**, in force from 13 October 2026 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The excerpts don't print the words "Authorised Version No.", so I'm relying on the version number in the file metadata.

## What the law says

- **Damage reports:** A renter must give the rental provider written notice, as soon as practicable, of damage to the premises [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Email counts [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Cleaning:** At the end of the agreement, you must leave the premises reasonably clean "as far as practicable". You must also leave them in the same condition as when you moved in, allowing for fair wear and tear [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The "as far as practicable" wording is relevant to your situation.
- **Damage you cause:** The duty not to damage the premises covers damage a renter or visitor causes intentionally or negligently [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The documents don't say who pays for damage done by burglars, so I can't answer that.
- **Urgent repairs:** The definition includes a burst water service, a blocked or broken lavatory system, a dangerous electrical fault, and a failure of the electricity or water supply. It also covers any fault or damage that makes the premises unsafe or insecure [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Whether your plumbing and wiring damage qualifies depends on the facts.
- **The provider's duty:** The standard agreement says the provider must carry out urgent repairs once notified. It also says only a suitably qualified person may do repairs [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

## What you can do or ask for

1. **Notify the provider or agent in writing now.** Describe the break-ins and the plumbing and wiring damage [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
2. **Ask for urgent repairs.** You may arrange them yourself only if you have taken reasonable steps to get the provider to do them immediately and they haven't [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - You must give the provider 7 days' written notice of the repairs and their cost [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - The provider must reimburse the reasonable cost within 7 days of that notice [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - The standard agreement summary puts the reimbursement cap at $2,500 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
3. **Apply to VCAT for an urgent repairs order** if you can't meet the cost, the cost is over the prescribed amount, or the provider refuses to pay. VCAT must hear the application within 2 business days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
4. **For non-urgent problems:** Give written notice. If the provider hasn't acted within 14 days, you can ask the Director to investigate or apply to VCAT. VCAT must hear that application within 7 days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
5. **Withhold rent through VCAT.** If you've given repair notice and the provider fails to repair, you can ask VCAT to authorise paying rent into the Rent Special Account [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
6. **Security:** The standard agreement requires the provider to ensure the premises have working window locks and deadlocks [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). If the provider unreasonably refuses consent to a lock change, you can apply to VCAT [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
7. **If the premises become unfit or unsafe, end the lease early.** You can give a notice of intention to vacate if the premises are unfit for human habitation, or destroyed to the extent of being unsafe. The termination date can be the date of the notice or later [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - The notice must be in writing and signed [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - The standard agreement for terms over 5 years says no "rent foregone" is payable when a renter ends the agreement under this section [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). I did not retrieve the matching wording for shorter agreements.
8. **Other ways out:**
   - You can end the lease by agreement with the provider [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - You can ask VCAT to shorten or end a fixed-term agreement for severe hardship caused by an unforeseen change in circumstances. VCAT may set compensation [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - An ordinary 28-day notice of intention to vacate has no effect on a fixed-term agreement if its termination date is before the end of the term [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

## Gaps

The documents don't cover insurance, police reports, bond deductions for burglar damage, or who bears the loss. I also can't tell whether your lease is fixed-term or periodic, or whether your own bags and cleaning make you liable for anything. For those questions, check with Consumer Affairs Victoria or a tenancy advice service.

I relied on the **Residential Tenancies Act 1997, Authorised Version No. 115** (file "rta-1997-v115-2026-10-13.pdf"). It incorporates amendments as at 13 October 2026 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). It is the latest version I retrieved, so I've treated it as the version in force today.

- **Cleaning and the bond:** A rental provider can claim from the bond "the reasonable cost of cleaning any part of the premises, if the premises were not left reasonably clean". The test takes into account the condition of the premises at the start of the tenancy [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Claim evidence:** Before a bond claim is made to the provider, they must give you bond claim evidence at least 3 days earlier. That evidence can be an invoice, receipt, quote or photograph, and it must not conflict with the condition report [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Claiming beyond the bond:** A person who has recovered compensation from a bond can still take proceedings under Part 5 to recover an additional amount [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). A party can apply to the Tribunal for compensation if the other party failed to meet their duties under the agreement or the Act [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The Tribunal may consider whether money has already been recovered, including from the bond [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Cleaning terms:** An agreement cannot require you to pay for professional cleaning unless that term is in the standard form [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

## Your two questions

**Is agreeing to a bond deduction the same as agreeing to pay an invoice?**
The Act doesn't say. I found nothing in the retrieved documents that treats the two as the same. The bond provisions deal with claims to the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). I found no provision making a separate invoice binding on you.

**Do you have to pay it?**
The documents don't say that an invoice sent after a full bond refund is automatically payable. They also don't say that it isn't. They also don't say whether the agent can claim cleaning costs after the bond has already been refunded in full. The Act gives the provider a route through the Tribunal, which can decide whether compensation is owed [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

## What you can do

1. **Ask for the evidence.** Request the invoice and any photos, and compare them with the condition report from the start of the tenancy [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
2. **Check reasonableness.** The cost must be reasonable, and the premises must actually have been left not reasonably clean, compared with how they started [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
3. **Check the cleaning term.** If the agreement required professional cleaning, check that the term was in the standard form [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
4. **Dispute it in writing** if you disagree. If the agent applies to the Tribunal, it decides whether compensation is payable [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

The premises must be **structurally sound and weatherproof**, and every room must be free from mould and damp caused by or related to the building structure. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf) The rental provider must also maintain the premises in good repair and in a fit condition for occupation. ## What you can do or ask

1. **Ask for repairs.** Give the rental provider written notice describing the damp, mould and rotting timber, and attach dated photographs. The condition-report form specifically allows you to record defects and repairs needed, and says that this gives written notice of the issue. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf)

2. **Seek an order requiring repairs.** If the repairs are non-urgent and are not completed within **14 days** after written notice, you may apply to the Director of Consumer Affairs Victoria for an investigation. [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) You may also apply to VCAT for specified repairs after that 14-day period; VCAT must hear the application within **7 days**. [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) VCAT may order specified repairs, require a suitably qualified person to do them, and award compensation. [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

3. **Do not simply stop paying rent or reduce it yourself.** The documents do not give you a right to unilaterally lower the rent. You may instead apply to VCAT for compensation, or—after giving a repair notice—seek an order allowing rent to be paid into the **Rent Special Account** while the repair breach continues. [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) If the breach concerns section 68 or the rental minimum standards and the repairs are still not done by the end of the ordered period, you may apply for some or all of that held rent to be paid to you. [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

**No.** You should not be charged a surcharge to pay rent electronically. **Yes, but in both cases charging you is likely unlawful:**

Based on Victorian residential tenancy law currently in force today (5 November 2026), here are your options regarding the damp, mould, and rotting timber you discovered. The relevant laws applied are the **Residential Tenancies Act 1997** (Authorised Version v115) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) and the **Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021** (Authorised Version v009) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

### 1. Can you cancel?
**Yes.** The Residential Tenancies Act 1997 explicitly provides for "Termination by renter before possession" [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Because damp, mould, and rotting timber are structural issues, the property likely breaches the mandatory rental minimum standards. Under the Regulations, rented premises must be structurally sound and weatherproof, and every room must be free from mould and damp caused by or related to the building structure [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). You can use these breaches as grounds to terminate the agreement before you officially move in.

### 2. Can you ask for repairs?
**Yes.** Your rental provider has a legal duty to maintain the premises in good repair and in a fit condition for occupation [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). To start this process:
* **Notify them immediately:** You must give written notice to the provider as soon as practicable about the damage [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). 
* **Urgent vs. Non-urgent:** If the damp or rotting timber poses an immediate health or safety risk (e.g., serious water ingress), it may be classified as an urgent repair, which the provider must fix immediately [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). For non-urgent repairs, the provider must act within a reasonable time [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
* **Escalation:** If they do not carry out non-urgent repairs within 14 days of your notice, you can apply to VCAT for an order requiring them to do the work [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

### 3. Can you ask for lower rent?
**You cannot unilaterally demand a rent reduction**, but you have a formal mechanism to pause or reduce your payments while repairs are pending:
* **Rent Special Account:** You can apply to VCAT for an order authorising you to pay your rent into a "Rent Special Account" instead of directly to the landlord [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). 
* **How it works:** VCAT will authorize this if they are satisfied that the provider has failed to comply with their repair duties or rental minimum standards, and that the provider cannot demonstrate financial hardship [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The money sits in the account until the repairs are completed or VCAT decides otherwise [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

**Recommended next steps:**

Based on the Victorian residential tenancy laws currently in force today (5 November 2026), here is your answer:

**Documents Applied:**
* *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021*, v009 (in force from 30 June 2026) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf)
* *Residential Tenancies Act 1997*, v115 (in force from 13 October 2026) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

### Do you have to pay for a professional cleaner?
**No.** Under the standard terms of your lease, an agent cannot blanket-require you to hire a professional cleaner unless:
1. Professional cleaning was actually carried out immediately before you moved in (and you were told about it); or
2. Professional cleaning is genuinely required to restore the carpets to the condition they were in at the start of your tenancy [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

Since you have already cleaned them yourself and they are back to how they were when you moved in, you have met your legal obligation. The law focuses on the *condition* of the property, not mandating a specific cleaning method [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). If professional cleaning isn't actually needed to restore the starting condition, demanding a receipt is unlawful [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

### What helps show the carpets' condition?
To prove you've left the carpets in the required state, rely on these official tools:
* **The Condition Report:** This form records the state of floor coverings at the start of your tenancy. You must be given two copies (or one emailed) to complete within 5 business days of moving in, and the agent must complete a final version within 10 days of you leaving [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
* **Dated Photos:** The condition report instructions explicitly advise taking photos of fixtures and fittings at both the start and end of the tenancy. You should attach these dated photos to the report, as they are highly useful in resolving disputes about the property's condition [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
* **Fair Wear and Tear:** Normal wear and tear is not considered damage under Victorian law, so the carpets do not need to look brand new—just in the same state relative to expected use as when you arrived [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

### If the agent still demands payment:
You can refuse to pay for professional cleaning you did not need. If the agent tries to claim this from your bond, they must provide evidence that does not conflict with your signed condition report [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). If they cannot prove the carpets were dirtier than at move-in (accounting for fair wear and tear), VCAT would likely dismiss their claim [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf), [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

### What the Law Says About Your Situation
- **Reporting damage:** The law requires you to give written notice to your residential rental provider as soon as practicable after becoming aware of any damage to the rented premises, including both the fact that it occurred and its nature [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). 
- **Maintenance duties:** Your landlord has a legal duty to ensure the rented premises are maintained in good repair [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). 
- **Uninhabitable premises:** If damage renders the property unsafe or unfit for human habitation, the law recognises this as a serious condition that affects your right to remain in the tenancy [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

### What You Can Do Before the Lease Ends
1. **Report the damage immediately**  
   Send written notice to your landlord/agent detailing the break-ins and the resulting plumbing and wiring damage [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). This can be done via electronic communication (e.g., email) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

2. **Arrange urgent repairs yourself (if necessary)**  
   If your landlord does not act, you may arrange for urgent repairs if:
   - You have taken reasonable steps to get them to fix it immediately, and
   - They are unable or unwilling to do so [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).  
   You must give your landlord 7 days' written notice of the repairs and costs. The landlord is legally required to reimburse you for the reasonable cost of these repairs within 7 days of receiving that notice [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

3. **Apply to the Tribunal if you cannot afford the repairs**  
   If the repair costs are too high for you to pay upfront, or if your landlord refuses to pay, you can apply to the Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal (VCAT) for an order requiring them to carry out the urgent repairs [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The Tribunal must hear this application within 2 business days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

4. **Terminate the lease early if the property is uninhabitable**  
   If the plumbing and wiring damage makes the premises unfit for human habitation or unsafe, you may give your landlord a notice of intention to vacate [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). You can choose to make this termination date the day you give the notice, or pick a later date [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). 

*(Note: Because the damage was caused by burglars rather than you or your visitors, you are not responsible for repairing it. Your primary legal obligations here are reporting the issue promptly and following the urgent repair/termination procedures outlined above.)*

Based on the retrieved Victorian residential tenancy documents currently in force, here is what the law says about your situation:

### 🔹 What the Law Says About Cleaning & Bonds
Under the **Residential Tenancies Act 1997**, a rental provider is only entitled to claim cleaning costs from your bond if the premises were not left reasonably clean [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Specifically, they may claim the *reasonable cost of cleaning* any part of the premises, provided this is compared against the condition of the premises when you moved in [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). 

You have a legal duty to leave the rented premises **reasonably clean** and in the same condition as when you started your tenancy, accounting for fair wear and tear [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

### 🔹 Rules on Professional Cleaning
The **Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021** strictly limit when a provider can require professional cleaning. They cannot demand it unless:
* Professional cleaning was carried out immediately before your tenancy started (and you were told this), or
* It is necessary to restore the premises to their original condition, considering the condition report and fair wear and tear [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

If professional cleaning *is* required under those conditions, the law states you must either have it done yourself or **pay the cost** of having it professionally cleaned [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

### 🔹 Do You Have to Pay the Separate Invoice?
The retrieved documents **do not explicitly address** whether agreeing to a bond deduction for cleaning is legally equivalent to agreeing to pay a separate invoice. The law only outlines what can be claimed from the bond and the conditions under which cleaning costs may be charged [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). It does not state that an agreement to deduct from the bond automatically waives your right to dispute a subsequent invoice, nor does it confirm that the two are legally interchangeable.

### 🔹 What You Can Do or Ask
1. **Request Evidence:** Under the Act, a rental provider must give you bond claim evidence supporting any deduction at least 3 days before making the claim [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). If they issued an invoice instead of claiming from the bond, ask them to clarify the legal basis for that charge and provide proof of the cleaning costs.
2. **Check Your Condition Report:** Compare the agent's cleaning claims against the condition report from when you moved in. They can only charge for cleaning beyond fair wear and tear [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
3. **Clarify the Agreement:** Ask the agent in writing whether your initial agreement was strictly for a *bond deduction* or if it explicitly included consent to pay a *separate invoice*. The documents do not define this distinction, so their own written terms will be key.
4. **Dispute if Unfair:** If you believe the invoice is unreasonable or duplicates a bond claim, you can raise a dispute with the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority (RTBA) or apply to VCAT for a determination [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

*Note: The above information is drawn from the Residential Tenancies Act 1997 (v115, in force 13 October 2026) and the Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021 (v009, in force 30 June 2026). For binding advice on contract interpretation or invoice disputes, consult a Victorian tenancy advocacy service or legal aid.*

- **A no-cost option must be available.** The provider or agent must ensure a rent payment method that incurs no additional costs (other than bank or account fees on the renter's own account) is reasonably available [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

- **The owner must pay you back.** The owner must reimburse the reasonable cost of the repairs, or the prescribed amount if it is less, within 7 days of receiving your written notice of the repairs and cost [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). This means any plumber you use should be properly qualified.

## What you can ask for

- **Tribunal order:** You can apply to VCAT for an order requiring the owner to carry out the urgent repairs if you cannot meet the cost, the cost is more than the prescribed amount, or the owner refuses to pay for repairs you arrange [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Under that version, the rental provider "must not require the renter to arrange professional cleaning or cleaning to a professional standard at the end of the tenancy" unless either (a) professional cleaning was done before the tenancy started and the renter was told so, or (b) professional cleaning "is required to restore the rented premises to the same condition they were in immediately before the start of the tenancy, having regard to the condition report and taking into account fair wear and tear" [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
- **Your situation:** Your lease clause (a pet clause requiring professional cleaning) doesn't override this. The regulations also say that where professional cleaning becomes required to restore the premises, the renter must have it done or pay for it [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). So the cost obligation only applies if professional cleaning is actually required under that test.
- **General duty:** At the end of a tenancy, a renter must leave the premises "as far as practicable" reasonably clean and "in the same condition as when the renter entered into possession of the premises, taking into account fair wear and tear" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf).

## What you can do or ask

1. **Check the start-of-tenancy condition report.** The regulations say the condition report "will help to resolve disputes over cleaning" and that photos should be taken at the beginning and end of the tenancy [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf). The version I retrieved is the 2022 form, so check it against the current form.
2. **Compare your end-of-tenancy photos** with any move-in photos. Photos should be dated and labelled by location [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).
3. **Ask the agent in writing** what condition they say the carpets are in, and whether they say professional cleaning is required to restore them to their move-in condition. This puts the question on record.
4. **Check whether the carpets were professionally cleaned before you moved in** and whether you were told. If not, the first exception in reg 12(1) doesn't apply [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
5. **Attend the final inspection if you can.** Under the 2022 form, the landlord must complete the final inspection and condition report within 10 days of the end date and give you a chance to attend [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).
6. **Seek help if they insist.** The Form 4 materials point renters to VCAT and to consumer.vic.gov.au/renting [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

- **A receipt requirement:** The documents I found don't say that you must provide a professional cleaner's receipt, or that a DIY clean can't count. They also don't define "professional standard."

- **Carpet-specific rules:** I found nothing specific to carpets.

## Important caveat about the Act

The Act text I retrieved (Residential Tenancies Act 1997, version 110) shows an end date of 24 November 2025 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf). This is general information, not legal advice. If the agent insists on payment, a free tenancy advice service such as Victoria Legal Aid or VCAT can review your specific lease and photos.

**1. A free payment method must be reasonably available (s 42(4)).** The rental provider or their agent must make sure a rent payment method with no additional costs is reasonably available to you. The penalty is 80 penalty units for a natural person and 400 for a body corporate [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

The penalty is 80 penalty units for a natural person and 400 for a body corporate [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

The standard-form agreement in the Regulations (version 009, from 30 June 2026) repeats that the rental provider "must permit at least one fee-free (other than the renter's own bank fees) payment method" [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

## Does it matter who receives the fee?

Partly, and the difference is in who each provision is aimed at:

- Sections 42(4) and 42(7) bind the rental provider and their agent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- Sections 51(3) and 51A apply to "a person". They aren't limited to the agent, so a fee kept by the app company could still be caught [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

The retrieved text doesn't say whether the answer changes depending on who keeps the fee.

## What you can do

- **Ask for the fee details in writing before you consent.** Section 42(7) entitles you to this [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Use the fee-free bank transfer.** You can pay that way, and the provider or agent must keep a fee-free method available [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Ask the agent to confirm which method is fee-free.** Their duty under s 42(4) is to make sure one is reasonably available [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Check your agreement.** Rent is payable in the manner the agreement specifies, and you and the provider can change that by agreement (s 42(2), (6)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The standard form has the provider tick the available payment methods [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

The retrieved documents don't cover where to complain or how to enforce these rules. For whether a particular card fee breaches s 51(3) or 51A, you would need the definitions and prescribed matters, which I didn't find. For that, check with Consumer Affairs Victoria or a tenancy advice service.

# Damp, mould and rotting timber before moving in (Victoria)

**Version used:** The current version is the *Residential Tenancies Act 1997* in the file "rta-1997-v115-2026-10-13.pdf", Version 115, in force from 13 October 2026 with no end date [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The retrieved text does not print an "Authorised Version No." on its face, so I'm taking "115" from the document's version metadata. I also used the *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021*, "rt-regs-2021-v009-2026-06-30.pdf", Version 009, in force from 30 June 2026 [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

## What the law says

- **Mould and damp can be an urgent repair.** "Urgent repairs" includes any fault or damage that makes the premises unsafe or insecure, including "the presence of mould or damp caused by or related to the building structure". It also includes a failure to comply with rental minimum standards [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Rotting timber** is not listed by name. It could be urgent if it makes the premises unsafe, and otherwise it would be a non-urgent repair. That is my reading, not something the documents state.
- **The rental provider must maintain the premises.** The duty to keep the premises in good repair sits in s 68. That section was not in the retrieved Version 115 text, but Version 115 refers to "the duty to maintain the rented premises in good repair" [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

## What you can do

**1. Ask for repairs (the clearest option)**
- Give the rental provider written notice of the damage as soon as practicable (s 72AA) [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **If it is urgent:**
  - You may arrange the repairs yourself if you took reasonable steps to get the provider or agent to do them immediately and couldn't [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
  - You must then give 7 days' written notice of the repairs and their cost [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
  - The provider must reimburse the reasonable cost, up to the prescribed amount, within 7 days of that notice [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The standard-form agreement summary states this as up to $2500 [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
  - You can apply to VCAT if you can't meet the cost, the cost is over the prescribed amount, or the provider refuses to pay. VCAT must hear the application within 2 business days [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **If it is not urgent:**
  - Give written notice. If the repairs aren't done within 14 days, you can ask the Director to investigate (s 74) [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
  - You can also apply to VCAT for a repair order (s 75). VCAT must hear it within 7 days [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
  - VCAT can order specific repairs by a suitably qualified person, with a deadline. It can also order compensation under s 212(2) [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Section 212 was not in the retrieved text, so I can't describe how compensation works.
  - VCAT will consider whether you caused the problem and whether the provider was notified and given a reasonable chance to fix it [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Keep documentary evidence such as photos [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

**2. Lower rent**
- The retrieved Version 115 text has no general right to a rent reduction.
- The closest tool is the **Rent Special Account**. After you give notice requiring repairs, you can ask VCAT to let you pay rent into that account. VCAT must make the order if the provider hasn't done the repairs and hasn't shown financial hardship (s 77) [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The rent is held, not reduced.
- You might also seek compensation (see above).

**3. Cancel the lease**
- The retrieved Version 115 text does not say you can cancel because of damp, mould or rotting timber. I won't guess at termination rights.
- An older version, Version 110 ("rta-1997-v110-2025-08-06.pdf", in force 6 August 2025 to 24 November 2025), contained ss 65 and 65A [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf). Both are **no longer the current version**.
  - Section 65 says you needn't take occupation, and needn't pay rent from the agreed move-in day until you actually move in, if the premises aren't vacant and reasonably clean. It says nothing about damp or mould [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf).
  - Section 65A requires the premises to meet the rental minimum standards by move-in. If they don't, you may request urgent repairs [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf).
  - I can't confirm from the retrieved Version 115 text that these sections are unchanged today.

## Not covered by the documents
The documents don't set out how to end the agreement, how a rent reduction works, or the rental minimum standards themselves. For those, check the current Act in full or contact Consumer Affairs Victoria or VCAT.

## What the law says

I used the versions in force today (6 November 2026). These are the *Residential Tenancies Act 1997*, file "rta-1997-v115-2026-10-13.pdf", dated 13 October 2026 and version 115 [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The other is the *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021*, file "rt-regs-2021-v009-2026-06-30.pdf", dated 30 June 2026 and version 009 [[8]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). Neither extract shows an "Authorised Version No." line. The numbers 115 and 009 come from the file titles and metadata.

- **Extra cleaning terms are restricted.** A rental agreement must not include a term requiring professional cleaning at the end of the tenancy, or requiring the renter to pay for it, unless that term is in the standard form [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). A prohibited term is void and unenforceable [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **The standard-form term is limited.** The provider must not require professional cleaning at the end of the tenancy unless one of two things applies [[8]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf):
  1. The premises were professionally cleaned immediately before the tenancy started, and the renter was told so. Or
  2. Professional cleaning is needed to restore the premises to the same condition as at the start, having regard to the condition report and allowing for fair wear and tear.
- **The renter's obligation matches this.** The renter must have the premises professionally cleaned, or pay for it, only if professional cleaning "becomes required" to restore them to their starting condition. That is judged against the condition report, with fair wear and tear allowed for [[8]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

## Applied to you

You say you cleaned the carpets yourself and they are back to how they were at move-in. On that basis, the second exception doesn't apply, and a professional clean isn't "required" [[8]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). You also wouldn't have to pay for one.

Check one thing: whether the carpets were professionally cleaned before you moved in, and whether you were told. If both are true, the first exception could apply [[8]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

A pet clause that demands professional cleaning regardless of condition looks broader than the standard-form term. It may therefore fall within the prohibited terms [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The retrieved documents say nothing specific about pet clauses, so I can't confirm that.

## What you can do or ask

- **Use the condition report.** The law ties the question to the condition report [[8]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). You should have been given 2 copies (or one emailed copy) on or before move-in [[8]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). Compare its carpet entries with the carpets now.
- **Ask the agent to say which exception they rely on.** Ask whether the carpets were professionally cleaned before your tenancy and you were told, or whether the condition report shows they need professional cleaning [[8]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
- **Challenge the term.** A renter may apply to the Tribunal for an order declaring a term invalid or varying it if it is harsh or unconscionable [[5]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

## What the documents don't cover

They don't list other evidence, such as dated photos or videos. They also don't say whether an agent can demand a cleaner's receipt. They only say professional cleaning can be required in the situations above [[8]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). Keeping your own dated evidence is sensible, but that is general advice and not something these documents state.

It is the current version, because it has no end date [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

## What the Act says about cleaning and bonds

- **Cleaning is a bond claim.** A provider (which includes their agent) may claim from the bond "the reasonable cost of cleaning any part of the premises, if the premises were not left reasonably clean by the renter". This is judged "having regard to the condition of the premises at the commencement" of the agreement [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) (s 411AB(1)(c)).
- **Evidence must come first.** At least 3 days before a claim for repayment of bond to the provider, the provider or agent must give each renter "bond claim evidence" that supports the claim [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) (s 411(1A)). That means an invoice, receipt, quote, photograph or other prescribed evidence [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The evidence must not conflict with a statement in a condition report [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) (s 411(1B)).
- **Claim forms must state amounts.** A provider must not request or obtain your signature on a bond claim form unless it states the amount of bond to be refunded and how it is apportioned. The penalty is 60 penalty units [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) (s 411(5)).
- **Your full refund.** The Authority must repay the bond if a provider or agent claims repayment of the bond to the renter [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) (s 411AC(b)).

## What the documents don't answer

- Nothing in the retrieved text deals with a separate invoice sent after the bond has been refunded.
- Nothing says that agreeing to a deduction from the bond also commits you to a separate invoice.
- Nothing says that the full refund ends the agent's right to claim.

On the face of the Act, cleaning costs are dealt with through a bond claim [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). That is not the same as a conclusion that the invoice can't be enforced.

## What you can do

1. **Ask the agent for the supporting evidence.** This means the photos, quotes or invoices, and the basis for the cleaning claim. Those are the types of evidence the Act lists for bond claims [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
2. **Compare it to the condition report.** The cleaning cost must relate to the condition at the start of the tenancy, and the evidence must not conflict with the condition report [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
3. **Check what you signed.** Look at whether the bond claim form specified the amount refunded and how it was apportioned [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
4. **Know the Tribunal route.** A renter can apply to the Tribunal about a bond claim. The application must be made within 14 days after the agreement terminated [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) (s 419A(2)). If that window has passed, the documents don't say what other options exist.

## What the law says

Today’s applicable documents are:

- **Residential Tenancies Act 1997, rta-1997-v115-2026-10-13.pdf**, **Authorised Version 115**, author **Barbara Hargreaves**, in force from 13 October 2026. [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)
- **Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021, rt-regs-2021-v009-2026-06-30.pdf**, **Authorised Version 009**, author **Lavina Mandy**, in force from 30 June 2026. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf)

The premises must be **structurally sound and weatherproof**, and each room must be free from mould and damp caused by or related to the building structure. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf) The rental provider must also maintain the premises in good repair and in a reasonably fit and suitable condition for occupation. [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

Mould or damp caused by the building structure is expressly an **urgent repair**; a failure to comply with rental minimum standards is also an urgent repair. [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) Rotting timber may also indicate that the premises are not structurally sound, but the documents do not classify every instance of rotting timber automatically as an urgent repair. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf)

## What you can do or ask

### 1. Cancel the agreement

If you **have not entered into possession**, section 91L allows you to give the rental provider a **notice of termination** because the premises:

- are not in good repair;
- are unfit for human habitation;
- do not meet rental minimum standards; or
- are otherwise unavailable for occupation. [[6]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf)

The documents do not define whether merely collecting the keys constitutes “entering into possession”. Therefore, they do not establish conclusively whether section 91L applies to your exact facts. [[6]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf)

You can also ask the rental provider to agree to end the agreement; an agreement may be terminated by mutual agreement. [[6]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/97-109aa110-authorised.pdf)

### 2. Ask for repairs

Give the rental provider or agent **written notice**, with dated photographs and a detailed list of the damp, mould and rotting timber. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf)

Because structural mould or damp and non-compliance with minimum standards are urgent repairs, you can request that they be dealt with urgently. [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) If the provider does not act, you may apply to the Tribunal for an order requiring urgent repairs; the Tribunal must hear that application within **2 business days**. [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

For non-urgent repairs, after written notice you may apply to the Director if repairs have not been completed within **14 days**. [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) You may then apply to the Tribunal for an order requiring the repairs, and the Tribunal must hear that application within **7 days**. [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

The Tribunal may order specified repairs, require a suitably qualified person to perform them, and order compensation under section 212(2). [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

### 3. Ask for lower rent or stop paying rent

You may ask the rental provider to agree to a lower rent, but the retrieved documents do **not** state a general statutory right to demand a rent reduction merely because repairs are needed.

You should not unilaterally stop paying rent. If the premises do not comply with the requirement to be vacant and reasonably clean on the agreed occupation day, you are not required to enter into occupation and are not required to pay rent for the period before you actually enter occupation. [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

If you have entered into occupation and the provider fails to carry out required repairs, you may apply to the Tribunal to pay rent into the **Rent Special Account** rather than directly to the provider. [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) If the Tribunal has ordered that rent be paid into that account because of a breach of the rental minimum standards and the repairs are still not done by the specified deadline, you may apply for all or part of that rent to be paid to you. [[7]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

**Practical course:** do not move in, do not treat the keys as accepting the condition, and immediately send written notice seeking either (a) termination under section 91L, or (b) urgent repairs and a written rent arrangement. The documents do not say that collecting the keys alone prevents termination, so that specific issue cannot be answered from them.

The current retrieved version is **Residential Tenancies Act 1997, Authorised Version 115, dated 13 October 2026**, authored by **Barbara Hargreaves**. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

A renter must leave the premises reasonably clean, considering their condition when the tenancy began. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) A rental provider may claim from the bond the **reasonable cost of cleaning** if the premises were not left reasonably clean. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

However, the retrieved Act does **not** say whether:

- agreeing that cleaning could be deducted from the bond is also an agreement to pay a separate invoice; or
- returning the full bond prevents the agent from later pursuing the cleaning cost separately.

So, based only on these documents, **I cannot say that you definitely have to pay the invoice, or that you definitely do not**. The documents do not answer that specific question. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

The Act treats a bond claim as a claim to the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority for repayment of all or part of the bond, including an apportionment between renter and rental provider. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) It also requires a rental provider seeking a bond claim to give supporting evidence at least **3 days before** making the claim. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) Those provisions do not expressly resolve a separate invoice issued after the full bond was repaid. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

## What you can do or ask

You can ask the agent to identify:

1. the legal or contractual basis for the separate invoice;
2. why the full bond was returned if they say cleaning costs were still owing;
3. the cleaning report, photos, condition report and itemised invoice; and
4. whether the amount claimed is limited to the **reasonable cost** of cleaning. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

You can state that you agreed only to a proposed **bond deduction**, not necessarily to a separate debt, and ask them to explain why they say the agreement has that wider effect. The retrieved documents do not establish whether that argument succeeds. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

If the matter becomes a dispute, the documents indicate that the Tribunal can determine applications concerning repayment of bond, but the retrieved material does not provide a rule deciding the separate-invoice issue. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)

Based on the *Residential Tenancies Act 1997* (Authorised Version No. 111) and the *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021* (Authorised Version No. 009), here is how Victorian tenancy law applies to your situation:

### **The Law**
Your rental provider or agent has strict legal obligations regarding how you pay rent:
- They must ensure that a payment method with **no additional costs** (other than your own bank fees) is reasonably available to you [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The standard tenancy agreement also explicitly notes that the provider must permit at least one fee-free payment method and allow Centrepay or electronic funds transfer [[6]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
- They must inform you of any costs you might incur before you agree to use a payment method, which explicitly includes **"third party transaction fees"** [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).

### **Can the app charge me a card fee?**
The legislation does not explicitly ban third-party apps from charging their own processing fees. However, it strictly requires your provider/agent to offer you a fee-free alternative (like the manual bank transfer option you found) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Because the law specifically calls out "third party transaction fees" as costs that must be disclosed, the app is permitted to charge a fee *provided* your agent has clearly told you about this cost before you agreed to use that payment method [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).

### **Does it matter whether the fee goes to the app company or the agent?**
No, the law does not distinguish based on who receives the fee. The focus of the legislation is entirely on two things: (1) ensuring a fee-free payment option is available to you, and (2) requiring full transparency about any costs—including third-party transaction fees—before you consent to a payment method [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). As long as your agent provides a free alternative and discloses the card fee upfront, the legal requirements are met regardless of whether the fee is kept by the app company or passed on to the agent.

*(Note: While Authorised Version No. 111 of the Act technically ended on 2026-06-29, the retrieved texts contain the operative provisions regarding payment methods applicable to your situation, and Version No. 009 of the Regulations is in force today [[6]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).)*

Based on the **Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021** (Authorised Version No. rt-regs-2021-v009), which is in force today, here is how the law applies to your situation:

### What the law says about professional cleaning
A rental provider cannot legally require you to arrange or pay for professional carpet cleaning unless one of two conditions is met [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf):
1. Professional cleaning was carried out immediately before you moved in, and you were explicitly advised that it had been done; **or**
2. Professional cleaning is genuinely required to restore the carpets to the same condition they were in when you moved in, taking into account fair wear and tear [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).

### Do you have to pay for a professional cleaner?
**No.** Since you have cleaned the carpets yourself and they are back to their original condition (accounting for normal wear and tear), professional cleaning is not required. The law only mandates paying for or arranging professional cleaning if it becomes necessary to restore the premises to their starting condition [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). A blanket clause in your lease demanding a receipt regardless of the actual state of the carpets is unenforceable under these regulations.

### What helps prove the carpets' condition?
To protect yourself from an unfair bond claim, rely on the **Condition Report** and photographic evidence:
* **Your signed Condition Report:** You should have received this at the start of your tenancy and were required to fill it out within 5 business days [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). Your copy serves as the baseline record of the carpets' original state. If you noted any disagreements or added comments about the carpet condition, keep that document safe [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).
* **Dated Photos:** Take clear, close-up photos of the carpets now (at move-out) that show they are clean and match their condition at the start of your tenancy. Ensure the photos are dated and clearly identify the location [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). 
* **The Final Inspection:** When you leave, the rental provider must complete a final inspection and fill out the end-of-tenancy section of the condition report within 10 days [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). They are legally required to allow for fair wear and tear, which does not count as damage [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

If the agent still demands a receipt, politely decline and provide your signed initial condition report alongside your dated move-out photos. If they attempt to deduct money from your bond based on this, you can dispute it with Consumer Affairs Victoria or apply to VCAT, where these documents will be the primary evidence used to determine liability [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

- **Owner's own tradespeople.** The documents don't say a rental provider can insist on using only their own tradespeople. This is my reading of the text, not an express rule in the documents.
- **Who does the work.** The standard rental agreement says only a suitably qualified person may do repairs, urgent or not. [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf) The Act defines "suitably qualified person" to include a tradesperson registered or licensed for the work, where the work requires it. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf) So use a licensed plumber rather than doing it yourself.

A prohibited term is void and unenforceable [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). An additional term that is a prohibited term is also invalid [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **The standard-form term is narrow.** The rental provider must not require professional cleaning unless one of two things applies [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf):

  2. Professional cleaning is needed to restore the premises to the same condition as at the start, having regard to the condition report and allowing for fair wear and tear.
- **You must pay only if cleaning is needed.** You must have the premises professionally cleaned, or pay for it, only if it becomes required to restore them to their starting condition, having regard to the condition report and fair wear and tear [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
- **Your general duty is lower.** At the end of the tenancy you must leave the premises reasonably clean and in the same condition as when you moved in, allowing for fair wear and tear [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

2. **Use photos.** The condition report form advises dated photos at the start and end of the tenancy. They must do it in your presence or give you a reasonable opportunity to be there [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). ## Source used
I used the **Residential Tenancies Act 1997**, file title "rta-1997-v115-2026-10-13.pdf", in force from 13 October 2026. Its metadata gives the version as **115**. I also used the **Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021**, file title "rt-regs-2021-v009-2026-06-30.pdf", dated 30 June 2026, version **009**. The metadata doesn't use the phrase "Authorised Version", so I'm giving the version numbers as they appear.

## What the law says

- **Reporting damage:** A renter must give the rental provider written notice of damage as soon as practicable [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Email is allowed [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Cleaning:** At the end of the agreement the renter must leave the premises reasonably clean "as far as practicable", and in the same condition as at move-in, allowing for fair wear and tear [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Because the test is "as far as practicable", damaged plumbing and wiring are relevant to what you can reasonably do.
- **Damage you cause:** A renter and their visitors must not intentionally or negligently damage the premises [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The documents don't say who is responsible for damage done by third-party burglars. I can't answer that from them.
- **Repairs:** The provider must keep the premises in good repair [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). "Urgent repairs" include a burst water service, a dangerous electrical fault, failure of the gas, electricity or water supply, and any fault or damage that makes the premises unsafe or insecure [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Damage from a break-in could fit these categories, depending on the facts.

## What you can do or ask for

1. **Notify the provider or agent in writing now**, describing the damage [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Include the break-ins and the plumbing and wiring damage.
2. **Ask for urgent repairs.** If you've taken reasonable steps to get the provider or agent to act immediately and they don't, you may arrange the urgent repairs yourselves [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - You must give the provider 7 days' written notice of the repairs and their cost [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - The provider must reimburse the reasonable cost within 7 days of that notice [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - The regulations' form of agreement states the direct reimbursement limit as $2,500 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
   - Only a suitably qualified person may do repairs, urgent or non-urgent [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
3. **Apply to VCAT (the Tribunal) for urgent repairs** if you can't meet the cost, the cost is over the prescribed amount ($2,500 per the form), or the provider refuses to pay [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf). The Tribunal must hear the application within 2 business days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
4. **For non-urgent repairs:** Give written notice. If the provider hasn't acted within 14 days, you can apply to the Director to investigate or to the Tribunal for an order [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The Tribunal must hear a non-urgent repairs application within 7 days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The Tribunal can also order rent to be paid into the Rent Special Account if repairs aren't done [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
5. **Consider ending the lease early.** A renter may give a written, signed notice of intention to vacate if the premises are unfit for human habitation or have been destroyed totally or to an extent that makes them unsafe [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The termination date can be the day you give the notice or later [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Without this ground, a notice under the general 28-day provision is of no effect on a fixed-term agreement if its termination date is before the end of the term [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
   - For fixed-term agreements of more than 5 years, the standard form says no "rent foregone" is payable when the renter ends the agreement on this ground [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf).
   - The documents don't define "unfit for human habitation". I can't say whether your premises meet that test.
6. **Agree an early end with the provider.** The agreement can be terminated by agreement of both parties [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

## Not covered
The documents don't say who is liable for the burglars' damage, how it affects your bond, or any insurance or police-report steps. I haven't answered those.

## What the law says

- **Your duty:** At the end of the tenancy you must leave the premises, as far as practicable, reasonably clean and in the same condition as when you moved in, allowing for fair wear and tear [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Cleaning and the bond:** A residential rental provider can claim from the bond "the reasonable cost of cleaning any part of the premises, if the premises were not left reasonably clean". The test is the condition of the premises when the tenancy started [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). A provider includes its agent for bond purposes [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Claiming beyond the bond:** A person who has recovered compensation from a bond can still take proceedings under Part 5 to recover an additional amount [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). Part 5 proceedings are applications to the Tribunal (VCAT). The Tribunal can order compensation if it is satisfied that compensation should be paid [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- **Money already recovered:** When it hears these applications, the Tribunal may consider whether money has already been paid or recovered, including from the bond [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

## Do you have to pay the invoice?

The Act has no provision making an agent's invoice payable on its own. The documents don't say that an agreement to a bond deduction is also an agreement to pay a separate invoice. The Act treats the two as separate routes:

- A bond claim is made to the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority on an approved form [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
- Anything beyond the bond is a compensation claim, and the Tribunal decides it [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

Your agreement was to a deduction from the bond. The full bond was returned, so nothing was actually taken for cleaning. Whether you owe anything depends on whether the premises weren't left reasonably clean and what the reasonable cost is [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). I can't tell that from the documents.

## What you can do or ask

1. **Ask for the evidence.** Before a bond claim, the provider or agent must give you "bond claim evidence" at least 3 days earlier. That means an invoice, receipt, quote, photograph or other prescribed evidence, and it must not conflict with the condition report [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
2. **Check the condition report.** Compare the cleaning charge with the condition report. A report signed by both parties is conclusive evidence of the premises' condition on the day it specifies, with some exceptions [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
3. **Check for a professional-cleaning term.** A term requiring you to pay for professional cleaning is prohibited unless it is in the standard form. The standard form allows it only where professional cleaning is needed to restore the premises to their starting condition, allowing for fair wear and tear [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).
4. **Dispute it.** Either party can apply to the Tribunal where there is a dispute under the agreement or a breach of the Act [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). The Tribunal's general monetary limit is $40,000 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf).

- They don't say whether your agreement to the deduction is binding as a contract or can be relied on to support the invoice.
- I didn't find a time limit for the agent to bring a cleaning compensation claim.
- Check the agent's claim against your agreement and the condition report, and consider contacting Consumer Affairs Victoria or VCAT before paying.

- The regulations prohibit a non-ADI from charging a fee for **rent payment**, including administrative costs and failed payments, but expressly exclude **payment surcharge fees permitted under another Act**. [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/21-3sra009-authorised.pdf)
